newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu mentor opposes system that elected him.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu mentor opposes system that elected him.

text.p: The man who brought Benjamin Netanyahu to political life said on Sunday he now wanted to change the electoral system by which his protege became Israel's prime minister.

"I am certainly for the idea of cancellation of the law for direct election of the prime minister," Moshe Arens, a former defence minister and now chairman of Netanyahu's Likud party's policy committee, told Israel Television.
"I think that it is a very damaging, very dangerous thing for the State of Israel."
Arens did not elaborate. Netanyahu's office was not immediately available to comment.
Israeli elections last May for the first time provided for direct election of the prime minister under a law that Netanyahu, 47, championed while a parliamentary back bencher.

The television said Arens had agreed to head an extra- parliamentary body dedicated to changing the law. A forum of members of parliament from both Likud and the main opposition Labour party is working toward the same goal.
Critics of the direct election system as it now stands say it gives too much power to the prime minister. Some Likud members have complained it allows the prime minister to ignore the party.
Netanyahu was introduced to Arens, who became his mentor, in the mid-1970s. He subsequently served as a diplomat in the Israeli embassy in Washington, his first political post, under Arens.
